theoretical_proofs.unipotent_resolvent_theorem: Theorem: Let L_c in R^{C x C} be strictly lower triangular with zero diagonal. Then (I - L_c) is unit lower triangular (unipotent). Its characteristic polynomial is det(lambda I - (I - L_c)) = (lambda - 1)^C. All C eigenvalues are identically 1.0, and det(I - L_c) = 1.0 identically for all keys, step sizes, and decay rates. Consequently, (I - L_c) is strictly non-singular and unconditionally invertible.
theoretical_proofs.adjoint_backward_theorem: Theorem: Let tilde_V_c = (I - L_c)^{-1} (diag(beta_c) V_c). For any scalar loss L with upstream gradient G = dL/d(tilde_V_c), the exact vector-Jacobian product is: dL/dV_c = diag(beta_c) * (I - L_c)^{-T} * G = diag(beta_c) * (I - L_c^T)^{-1} * G. Because L_c is strictly lower triangular, (I - L_c^T) is unit upper triangular. The linear system (I - L_c^T) X = G is solved via reverse backward substitution: X_i = G_i + sum_{j=i+1}^C (L_c)_{ji} X_j in exactly O(C^2 d_v) operations, without materializing matrix inverses or incurring numerical drift.
